summary: ```markdown # CLO 2025.1 - Upgraded 3D Pen ## Introduction This video introduces the upgraded 3D pen virtual model function and its related function updates. ## Drawing in the 3D Environment First, you can draw in the area outside the model. You can directly draw the clothing version in the 3D environment without having to start from the 2D version. You can not only draw the curve on the model surface, but you can also freely draw in the surrounding 3D environment. This functionality makes it easier to build complex three-dimensional outlines. ### Re-Creating the Outline Now, let's re-create the outline of the chest according to the reference clothing. You can directly see how to use the function after upgrading. 1. **Select the Tool**: First, select the 3D pen virtual model tool. When you select it, a line of hints will appear next to the light. 2. **Placing the Model**: You can click on the model to place it. 3. **Creating a Template**: Press the P key to create a template outside the model surface. In this example, I will start from the model surface and extend outward to create a three-dimensional skirt. ## Drawing with the 3D Pen Let's start by using the 3D pen. Draw a curve along the model's body. Now, let's draw the 3D version. Here, I will press the P key. This function allows you to copy the model and freely extend the line to the 3D environment. ### Guide Points At the same time, a guide point will appear to let you directly check the X, Y, and Z axes. - **Blue** represents the Z axis, - **Red** represents the X axis, - **Green** represents the Y axis. Just like drawing on the model, when you are drawing in the 3D area, you can also press the Ctrl key to draw a curve. To improve accuracy, when you are drawing in the 3D environment, you can also press the Shift key. This will create 8 guide points at 45 degrees in the 3D window. Your view and mouse cursor will automatically align with these guides, allowing you to draw more accurately in the 3D environment. Once you release the Shift key, the guide will disappear. ### Displaying Distance Next, press the D key to show a curve and display the actual distance between the mouse pointer and the model. Press the D key again to close the function. ## Completing the Drawing When you have completed the drawing in the 3D area, click the point where you first drew and the area where you drew. Click and press the 3D pen to display the tool. Then, select the flat version tool. A tool will appear next to your cursor, prompting you to select the area to be generated. Press the return key to select a section of your version. In this way, a flat version will be generated in the 3D window, and you can see it in the 2D window at the same time. ## Advantages of the Upgraded 3D Pen Using the 3D pen virtual model function after upgrading allows you to draw directly in the 3D area, both outside and on the model. This feature enables you to draw faster in the design process and combine multiple dimensions to create the flat version you want, helping you to create the complex designs you imagine more easily. ### Selection and Display Options Next, I will introduce to you other advantages of the 3D pen virtual model. 1. **Selecting Lines**: You can use the 3D pen virtual model tool to select the line in the 3D window by pressing the drag and drop button. You can also use the shortcut Ctrl + A to select all the lines. 2. **Display Length Option**: In the menu of the 3D line, pressing the right button will increase the option of display length. After pressing the cancel option in the blank, it will not display and only show in the selected state. If you need to hide it, you can use the same operation to hide the measurement length. ### Copying 3D-Painted Lines The next update is that the 3D-painted line can be copied to the edge of the grid. This function allows the 3D pen line to be automatically copied along the virtual model grid path, improving the accuracy and speed of creation or adjustment of the version. When using this option, the line will be aligned with the recent grid edge. ## Merging Multiple Sheets Now, in addition to being able to 3D paint multiple sheets at a time, you can also merge them into one. 1. **Selecting Multiple Areas**: First, select multiple closed areas and press the return button directly. You can see that there are multiple sheets that have been sewn in the 2D window. 2. **Deleting a Sheet**: Delete the sheet. Now, when I operate again, you will see that the 3D pen is now 3D. You will see the tool prompt that you need to press the Shift and return keys. At this time, there is only one sheet in the 2D window. This improvement greatly simplifies the work of converting the 3D block into a 2D sheet, speeding up the process and reducing manual operation. ```
